items.title: NPP will negotiate with popular non-politicians to secure winnable candidates – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it will engage popular individuals who are not active in politics as part of efforts to identify potential parliamentary candidates ahead of the 2028 general elections. NPP Director of Communications Dennis Miracles Aboagye said the party is assessing constituencies to identify individuals with the strongest potential to secure parliamentary seats for the party. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story, he said some popular figures within communities may not have considered entering politics but could be encouraged to contest if the party determines that they have the support needed to win. “The party has already started conversations long before now on ensuring that for every constituency, a proper calibration is done to identify person or persons who have the biggest capacity or chance to win the election,” he said. Mr Aboagye explained that the strategy could also involve discussions with previous NPP parliamentary candidates who narrowly lost the 2024 elections, particularly where internal disagreements may have affected the party’s performance. He said the party would consider the dynamics of each constituency rather than applying a uniform approach to the selection of parliamentary candidates. “There are some constituencies when you go, you identify about four or five capable people. What it means is that all of four or five of them have the capacity to win the seat. You have to put them into the ballot,” he said. He added that in other constituencies, the party could engage popular individuals, including those without political backgrounds, and encourage them to contest where they are considered capable of winning the seat. Mr Aboagye said the approach forms part of the strategy outlined by NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, who has disclosed that the party has begun scouting for potential parliamentary candidates ahead of the 2028 elections.

items.title: Only 5% of Ghanaians can afford housing without support – Gov’t
items.description: The government says only about five per cent of Ghanaians can afford to secure housing without assistance. According to the government, about 60 per cent of the population requires state-facilitated support to access decent housing, while another 30 per cent remains unable to secure housing even with government subsidies. The figures were contained in a joint statement issued by the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources and the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs to mark World Habitat Day 2026. The observance was held under the theme “Adequate Housing for All.” The ministries said the country’s housing challenge was being driven by several factors, including high land prices, rising construction and infrastructure costs, and limited access to affordable housing finance. “These realities underscore the need for deliberate interventions to make housing more accessible and affordable to all,” the ministries stated. As part of efforts to address the housing deficit and improve access to homeownership, the government is implementing the National Mortgage Scheme in partnership with the National Housing Fund and Republic Bank. Under the scheme, mortgage financing is available at an interest rate of approximately 8.4 per cent per annum, with repayment periods of up to 20 years. The ministries said the initiative was designed to support Ghanaians who have traditionally been excluded from the formal mortgage market. They said the scheme would provide more people with an opportunity to own decent homes by improving access to relatively affordable long-term mortgage financing. Beyond mortgage financing, the government is also implementing broader policies aimed at addressing housing and urban development challenges. These include the National Urban Policy and Implementation Plan 2026–2035 and the National Slum Upgrading and Prevention Strategy and Implementation Plan 2026–2035. The ministries said the policies were intended to provide a more coordinated approach to housing, urban development and the improvement of living conditions in communities. They stressed, however, that adequate housing should not be measured simply by the number of houses constructed. According to the ministries, decent housing must also provide access to essential services and infrastructure, including potable water, sanitation, roads, electricity, drainage and public spaces. The government said tackling Ghana’s housing challenge would require sustained investment and targeted interventions, particularly for households that cannot afford homes through conventional means. It reiterated its commitment to expanding access to housing while improving the conditions in existing communities. “Government remains committed to expanding access to decent, affordable and sustainable housing throughout the country,” the ministries stated.

items.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
items.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh. The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said. “The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” it added. While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict. In the Riyadh meeting, the three members of the Makkah Defence Alliance condemned “in the strongest terms” the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madina, as well as the continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the kingdom’s security and territorial integrity”, the statement said. For their part, Pakistan and Turkiye commended the “vigilance and readiness of the Saudi armed forces, as well as the professionalism and high level of competence they have demonstrated in countering the threats and attacks facing the kingdom and in safeguarding its security and territorial integrity”, the FO said. The SPDC reviewed the outcomes of the political and military consultations preceding the meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it, affirming that the Makkah pact embodied a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats, it said. Moreover, the three countries affirmed that the security of each member of the alliance was an “integral part of the collective security of the three countries, and that translating the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence into practical measures demonstrates the credibility of the commitment to collective defence, strengthens the effectiveness of deterrence, and reaffirms the unity and determination of our three countries to defend their security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement”. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis. When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. “Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance. The defence minister said the meeting was primarily focused on formalising the Makkah alliance’s operational structure. “The organisational structure of the alliance was formalised during today’s meeting,” he said. As part of the institutional development of the Makkah alliance, the SPDC decided to appoint Pakistan’s Lieutenant General (Retd) Nauman Mahmood as the first secretary general of the alliance for a three-year term, the FO statement said. “The parties welcomed him, wished him every success in the discharge of his duties, and expressed their confidence in his contribution to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives,” it added. In an earlier statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) included Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Asif. “The meeting will also be attended by the respective ministers of foreign affairs, ministers of defence, as well as chiefs of general staff of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the Republic of Türkiye,” the FO added. The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. The SPDC meeting under it has been held as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating over the weekend, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on Yemen’s capital Sanaa, after which they attacked an Aramco facility with ballistic missiles and drones south of Riyadh. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait in a lightning offensive. On Sept 25, the military chiefs of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. On Sept 18, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry had expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. Defence Minister Asif also earlier reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated.

items.title: Octobre Rose : Ooredoo Tunisie transforme chaque pas en un geste solidaire avec Go Run
items.description: À l’occasion d’Octobre Rose, Ooredoo Tunisie se mobilise une nouvelle fois dans la lutte contre le cancer du sein en lançant, en partenariat avec Go Run, un challenge solidaire ouvert à tous. Tout au long du mois d’octobre, les participants sont invités à marcher, courir et cumuler des points via Go Run. Cette initiative associe activité physique et engagement solidaire, en soutenant le don d’Ooredoo Tunisie au profit de l’Association Tunisienne d’Assistance aux Malades du Cancer du Sein (ATAMCS) et de ses actions en faveur des femmes touchées par la maladie. Le challenge invite ainsi chacun à transformer ses efforts quotidiens en un élan collectif de solidarité, tout en sensibilisant à l’importance de la santé, de la prévention et du dépistage. Les participants pourront cumuler des points en fonction de leur activité tout au long de la campagne, avec à la clé un prix de 2 500 TND pour le participant ayant obtenu le meilleur score. Organisé du 1er au 31 octobre 2026, le challenge est accessible via *411#, My Ooredoo et la plateforme Go Run. À travers son programme RSE Tounes T3ich, Ooredoo Tunisie poursuit son engagement en faveur d’initiatives qui mobilisent la communauté autour de la santé et d’un impact social positif. items.title: 10 oldest universities in Africa
items.description: By Mmesoma Goodness African universities have a long and rich history of scholarship, with some of the continent’s most important centres of learning dating back more than 1,000 years. Some of these institutions began as mosques, madrasas and centres of Islamic scholarship before evolving into institutions recognised as universities in the modern era. Others began as colleges or higher-education institutions during the 19th century and later acquired full university status. Because of these differences, the ranking below is based broadly on the earliest documented origins of the institution or educational tradition that developed into the present-day institution, rather than strictly on the date when each institution acquired modern university status. Here are 10 of Africa’s oldest universities and higher-learning institutions. 1. Ez-Zitouna University — Tunisia Educational origins: 737 AD Ez-Zitouna University in Tunis traces its educational history to the Great Mosque of Ez-Zitouna, where Islamic sciences were being taught from around 737 AD, according to the university’s official history. The mosque itself dates to an earlier period, with the university describing it as having been founded in 734 AD. Over the centuries, Ez-Zitouna became an important centre of Islamic scholarship, teaching subjects including Islamic jurisprudence, Quranic studies and Arabic. The institution’s modern university structure is much more recent, but its long educational tradition is why Ez-Zitouna is frequently included among Africa’s oldest centres of higher learning. 2. University of Al-Qarawiyyin — Morocco Founded: 859 AD The University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez is traditionally dated to 859 AD, when Fatima al-Fihri established the institution that developed around the Al-Qarawiyyin mosque. It became an important centre of Islamic and Arabic scholarship and attracted scholars and students from across the Muslim world. Al-Qarawiyyin is widely recognised as one of the world’s oldest continuously operating institutions of higher learning. However, as with several institutions on this list, its early form was different from the modern university system that developed centuries later. 3. Al-Azhar University — Egypt Origins: 970–972 AD Al-Azhar University in Cairo traces its origins to the Al-Azhar Mosque, whose construction began after the Fatimid conquest of Egypt. The first Friday prayer at the mosque was held in 972 AD. Al-Azhar subsequently developed into a major centre of Islamic scholarship, particularly in theology, Islamic law and Arabic studies. Although its modern university structure developed much later, Al-Azhar’s more than 1,000-year history as a centre of learning makes it one of Africa’s most historically significant educational institutions. 4. Sankore and the Historic Centres of Learning in Timbuktu — Mali Major period of scholarship: 14th–16th centuries Timbuktu should not be listed as a “University of Timbuktu founded in 982 AD.” There is no reliable historical basis for that specific founding date. Instead, Timbuktu is better described as a historic centre of higher learning , particularly through institutions associated with the Sankore, Djingareyber and Sidi Yahia mosques. UNESCO describes Timbuktu as an intellectual and spiritual capital of Africa during its 15th and 16th-century golden age , with the University of Sankore and other madrasas playing a major role in Islamic scholarship. Sankore became particularly renowned for scholarship in areas including Islamic law, literature, mathematics, astronomy and other fields of knowledge. Historical accounts associate Timbuktu with a large network of scholars, students and manuscript collections. The city therefore deserves a place in a list of Africa’s oldest centres of higher learning, but not with the incorrect 982 AD founding date . 5. Fourah Bay College — Sierra Leone Founded: 1827 Fourah Bay College in Freetown was founded on 18 February 1827 by the Church Missionary Society. The University of Sierra Leone describes it as the first Western-style university institution established in sub-Saharan Africa. The college was originally established to train teachers and missionaries. In 1876, it became a degree-granting institution through its affiliation with Durham University in England. In 1967, Fourah Bay College became a constituent college of the University of Sierra Leone. Its nearly two-century history makes it one of the most important landmarks in the development of Western-style higher education in Africa. 6. University of Cape Town — South Africa Origins: 1829 The University of Cape Town (UCT) traces its origins to 1829, when the South African College was established in Cape Town. The college initially combined secondary and tertiary education. It expanded considerably during the late 19th and early 20th centuries and eventually developed into a fully fledged university. UCT was formally established as a university in 1918. The institution is now one of Africa’s leading research universities and remains South Africa’s oldest university. Thus, while 1829 is used to describe UCT’s historical origins, the university in its formal modern form dates from 1918. 7. University of Liberia — Liberia Origins: 1862 The University of Liberia was established in 1862 as Liberia College. According to the university’s official history, Liberia College opened its doors to students in February 1863, with seven students in its first group. It became a full university in 1951. The institution was established during the early years of the Liberian republic to provide higher education and help develop the country’s professional and intellectual class. Today, the University of Liberia is a public university with campuses and programmes covering a range of academic disciplines. 8. Stellenbosch University — South Africa Origins: 1866 Stellenbosch University’s educational roots can be traced to the Stellenbosch Gymnasium, established in 1866. The institution subsequently evolved through several stages, becoming a college and later Victoria College before achieving full university status. Stellenbosch University was officially established as a university on 2 April 1918, alongside the University of Cape Town and the University of South Africa. The university therefore has a distinction between its 1866 educational origins and its 1918 formal university status. It has since grown into one of South Africa’s major research universities, with strengths across science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, the humanities and social sciences. 9. University of South Africa — South Africa Origins: 1873 The University of South Africa (Unisa) traces its history to the University of the Cape of Good Hope, established in 1873 by an act of the Cape Colony’s Parliament. The institution was modelled on the University of London and initially served largely as an examining and academic standards body for affiliated colleges. It was renamed the University of South Africa in 1916. Unisa later developed into a major distance-learning institution. Its transition to distance education became particularly significant in the 20th century, and it is now one of the world’s largest open-distance learning universities. Therefore, 1873 represents the origin of the institution’s predecessor rather than the establishment of Unisa under its present name. 10. Cairo University — Egypt Founded: 1908 Cairo University traces its origins to the Egyptian University, which was inaugurated on 21 December 1908 as a private university. The institution was later incorporated into the state university system. In 1925, the government established a state university under the name Egyptian University, incorporating the earlier institution and several higher schools. The university was subsequently known as Fuad I University before becoming Cairo University. It has played a major role in Egyptian education, research and intellectual life and remains one of the country’s leading universities. items.title: Salary arrears: SSANU ‌‍⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠‍‌gives FG 14-day ultimatum, threatens indefinite strike
items.description: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has given the Federal Government a 14-day ultimatum to pay outstanding salary arrears. SSANU National President, Mr Mohammed Ibrahim, announced the ultimatum in a communique issued on Monday in Abuja, after the union’s 56th National Executive Council (NEC) meeting. Ibrahim said that the meeting, held at the University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom, from Sept. 30 to Oct. 1, deliberated on workers’ welfare, university funding and implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU Agreement. He said failure to meet the demand within the stipulated period would compel the union to embark on an indefinite strike without further notice. He said the NEC demanded immediate payment of all outstanding arrears arising from implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU CONTTA salary structure, effective from Jan. 1, 2026. “NEC categorically demanded the immediate release and payment of all outstanding arrears arising from the implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU CONTTA salary structure, calculated from the effective date of Jan. 1, 2026,” he said. Ibrahim said some universities had implemented the salary structure largely through internally sourced funds, without direct financial backing from the Federal Government. He urged Vice-Chancellors and Governing Councils of universities that were yet to implement the agreement to emulate institutions that had taken proactive steps toward compliance. The SSANU president also demanded immediate payment of two months’ salaries withheld during the 2022 industrial action, alongside one-year arrears from the 25 per cent and 35 per cent salary increases. Ibrahim described the outstanding payments as “legitimate entitlements” owed to affected workers, saying, “continued delay had worsened the financial hardship confronting members”. He expressed concern over uneven implementation of the agreement in state-owned universities and called on state governments to provide the necessary funding for full compliance. On university funding, Ibrahim called for increased investment in electricity, laboratories, workshops, libraries, ICT facilities, security systems and infrastructure maintenance, while rejecting virtual accreditation as a substitute for physical verification. He also rejected any arrangement to concede, privatise or transfer management of King’s College, Lagos, or other public educational institutions to private bodies, urging government to preserve public ownership and accessibility. Ibrahim further expressed concern over insecurity, rising living costs and food insecurity. He called for stronger protection of farming communities and educational institutions, including policies to protect workers’ incomes. (NAN) The post Salary arrears: SSANU ‌‍⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠‍‌gives FG 14-day ultimatum, threatens indefinite strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria launches rescue after military plane crashes with 32 aboard
items.description: Nigeria has launched a search-and-rescue operation after a military aircraft carrying 32 people crashed in Ondo State in the country’s southwest. The wreckage of the aircraft has been located near the naval base in Igbokoda, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said on Monday. The plane disappeared while flying from Benin to Lagos. “The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Keyamo said in a statement on social media. He added that preliminary information indicated that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board. Air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at 09:13 local time (0813 GMT). Repeated attempts to reach it by radio were unsuccessful. INFORMATION ON CRASH OF A MILITARY AIRCRAFT I regret to inform the general public that Air Traffic Controllers have informed me of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today. All efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive. Subsequently information however confirmed that the military aircraft has crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing. Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board. Whilst the control and regulation of military aircraft are completely outside the authority of the Ministry of Aviation, and Civil Aviation Authority, I have just spoken to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke and pledged our total cooperation and assistance in the search and rescue efforts ongoing. Further information on this unfortunate incident will be made available subsequently. — Festus Keyamo, SAN, CON, FCIArb (UK) (@fkeyamo) October 5, 2026 The Nigerian air force said the plane was an ATR-42 that had been travelling to Lagos on a routine flight. Rescue teams have been deployed to the crash site. Keyamo said he had spoken with Nigeria’s Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and offered the Aviation Ministry’s “total cooperation and assistance” in the rescue effort. Authorities have not yet confirmed any casualties, and it was not immediately clear how badly the aircraft was damaged.

items.title: GES digitalisation already exists; restore discontinued platforms – Adutwum spokesperson
items.description: A spokesperson for former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has challenged claims that the Ghana Education Service (GES) still relies heavily on manual processes, insisting that several digital platforms to address such challenges were introduced years ago. In a statement signed by Yaw Opoku Mensah, spokesperson for Dr Adutwum, the former minister’s office said the digital systems being advocated by the current Education Minister had already been developed and implemented within the GES. The statement called for the restoration and improvement of the platforms, rather than the introduction of new systems to address challenges that had already been tackled. “The digitalisation the Minister is advocating already exists within GES. What is required now is its restoration, sustained use and further improvement,” the statement said. The response follows comments by the current Education Minister in a video about manual data entry within the GES. According to Mr Opoku Mensah, those comments risk creating the impression that the Service had not previously undertaken significant digital reforms. He said GES began its digital transformation efforts in 2017 with the aim of reducing paperwork, improving data management and speeding up service delivery. Among the platforms introduced were the GES Recruitment and Promotions platforms, Smart Workplace, the Self-Placement Recruitment Platform and the Ghana Education Service Management Information System (GESMIS). The statement said the recruitment and promotions platforms were designed to simplify staff administration and reduce delays in processes affecting teachers and other GES employees. The systems allowed promotions and related administrative matters to be processed more efficiently while reducing the need for staff to repeatedly submit supporting documents. “These reforms directly addressed delays and paperwork in services affecting staff welfare and career progression,” the statement said. The former minister’s spokesperson argued that these systems demonstrated that digitalisation had already been applied to key areas of GES administration. The statement also highlighted the Self-Placement Recruitment Platform, which was introduced in 2024. It said the platform allowed newly recruited teachers to select their preferred regions, districts and schools before printing their appointment letters online. According to the statement, more than 12,000 newly recruited teachers across the country used the platform to print their appointment letters in less than four hours. The spokesperson said the exercise demonstrated how digital platforms could reduce administrative pressure while giving teachers greater control over their placements. “This platform demonstrated the capacity of digital systems to simplify recruitment and placement, reduce administrative burdens and give teachers greater choice over where they would work,” the statement said. The statement also pointed to Smart Workplace, which it said was introduced to digitise internal communication and administrative processes at the GES headquarters. The platform allowed memos, correspondence and other official communications to be processed electronically, reducing the need to move physical files between offices. It added that customised official email accounts were also introduced for GES staff, beginning at the headquarters, with plans to extend the system progressively to the school level. The initiative, according to the statement, was intended to reduce dependence on paper-based communication and improve the speed of official business within the Service. Another major digital initiative cited in the statement is the Ghana Education Service Management Information System (GESMIS). The system was designed to improve the collection, processing and management of data from schools through district and regional offices to the GES headquarters. The statement said GESMIS was intended to reduce repeated manual data entry and provide a coordinated system for administration and decision-making across the Service. It added that Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum officially launched GESMIS in 2024 as part of efforts to improve efficiency, transparency, accountability and service delivery. The spokesperson stressed that the various reforms were not merely proposals but had already been implemented. “All these achievements are documented in the official handing-over notes to the current Director-General of the Service,” the statement said. Mr Opoku Mensah said the current debate should distinguish between the absence of digital systems and the discontinuation of systems that had already been developed and put into use. He argued that the platforms had been created specifically to reduce the administrative burdens that staff and stakeholders were now experiencing. “GES had already established platforms to address these processes. Their use has since been discontinued, bringing back the administrative burdens they were introduced to reduce,” the statement said. The spokesperson said digital transformation required continuity, arguing that systems must be maintained and staff supported to use them effectively. “Digital transformation requires continuity. Platforms must be maintained, staff must be supported to use them, and implementation challenges must be resolved,” he said. He further cautioned against presenting the return of manual processes as evidence that digitalisation had never been undertaken within GES. “Discontinuing their use and then presenting the resulting manual processes as evidence that digitalisation has yet to begin gives an incomplete account of the institution’s progress,” the statement added. The former minister’s spokesperson called on the Education Ministry and GES leadership to investigate why the platforms were no longer being used and take steps to restore them. He said technical and administrative problems affecting the systems should be identified and addressed, while improvements could be made to the existing platforms where necessary. “The immediate task is to establish why these platforms are no longer being used, restore their operation and address any technical or administrative gaps,” the statement said. “Where improvements are needed, the existing systems provide a foundation to build on.” The statement also urged the current Education Minister to examine the official handing-over notes and engage the officers who were responsible for implementing the reforms. “The Minister should review the handing-over notes, engage the officers responsible for implementing these reforms and obtain a full briefing on the platforms’ functions and current status,” it said. According to the spokesperson, such a review would help the Ministry identify the resources and interventions needed to restore and strengthen the systems rather than starting the digitalisation process from scratch. He said continuity was particularly important for GES staff and other stakeholders who rely on the Service’s administrative systems. “GES staff and stakeholders deserve continuity in service delivery. Ghanaians also deserve an explanation of why established digital platforms have been discontinued,” the statement concluded.

items.title: Police launch manhunt for 7 after deadly Bunkprugu violence
items.description: Police in Bunkprugu in the North East Region have launched a manhunt for Melchizedek Babotin Musah and six others following a deadly escalation in the town’s protracted chieftaincy dispute. The renewed violence erupted on Saturday after Mr Musah was allegedly enskinned as a rival chief by members of the Jamong Family at a secluded location, despite a court injunction restraining the group from proceeding with the ceremony. The development was followed by clashes between rival factions later in the day, leaving a woman dead and a soldier injured after gunmen reportedly opened fire on a military vehicle responding to the disturbance. The injured soldier was rushed to a hospital in Bolgatanga for treatment. The police say those behind the enskinment fled Bunkprugu shortly afterward and are now being pursued, the police said. The incident marks a fresh and potentially dangerous escalation in the decades-old chieftaincy dispute between the Jamong and Jafouk families since 2016. Enskinment despite injunction The police had on September 9 secured an injunction against Nyanu Yogbat and six others, restraining them from going ahead with plans to enskin a rival chief. The legal action followed an earlier attempt on August 18, which was halted after the North East Regional Security Council intervened to prevent the ceremony from taking place. Despite the court order, members of the Jamong Family reportedly proceeded with the ceremony on Saturday at an undisclosed location, where Melchizedek Musah was allegedly installed as their chief. The group reportedly left the area immediately after the ceremony. Tensions escalated later in the evening when rival factions clashed, leading to gunfire and the death of a woman. Security personnel who moved in to restore order also came under attack, with gunmen reportedly firing at a military vehicle. One soldier sustained a gunshot wound in the attack and was subsequently evacuated to Bolgatanga for medical attention. Long-running chieftaincy dispute The latest violence is rooted in a long-running dispute over the Bunkprugu traditional leadership. The Jamong Family has, following its victory at the National House of Chiefs, been pushing for the removal of the incumbent chief, Naa Abuba Nasinmong of the Jafouk Family. The National House of Chiefs earlier this year ruled on the decades-old dispute, with the decision reportedly favouring the Jamong Family. The House subsequently directed the family to engage the Mamprugu Overlord for the necessary traditional remedies. Naa Abuba Nasinmong, however, appealed the decision. The Nayiri, who is the enskinning authority, has reportedly reaffirmed his support for Naa Nasinmong, adding another layer to the dispute. The competing claims over the traditional leadership have since generated tensions and repeated attempts by the rival factions to assert their positions. Police launch manhunt Speaking to JoyNews’ North East Regional Correspondent, ASP Emmanuel Simtim confirmed that the police were actively searching for those allegedly behind the latest incident. “We are now looking for them,” he said. ASP Simtim added that investigations were ongoing to identify those responsible for the violence. “Investigation is still ongoing to find out the culprits,” he said. The police commander said calm had since returned to Bunkprugu and that the situation was under control. However, the latest incident has raised fresh concerns about the potential for further violence if the competing claims to the Bunkprugu chieftaincy are not resolved through the appropriate legal and traditional processes. The police added that they are continuing investigations into the alleged breach of the injunction, the reported rival enskinment, the death of the woman and the shooting of the soldier.

items.title: GTEC directs UDS to immediately cease unauthorised mode of delivering accredited LLB programme
items.description: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has directed the University of Development Studies (UDS) to cease with immediate effect, the delivery of the accredited evening LLB programme as a weekend programme and to restore the programme to its duly approved evening mode of delivery. Subsequently, GTEC has directed UDS to immediately discontinue any arrangement requiring students admitted to the evening programme to convert to weekend delivery. Again, the university is to ensure that all affected students are restored to the approved mode of delivery without academic or financial disadvantage. It is also to communicate the Commission’s directive formally to all affected students and relevant academic and administrative units; and submit to the Commission, within seven (7) days, documentary evidence demonstrating full compliance with this directive. A failure to comply with this directive within seven (7) days may result in regulatory action without further notice to the university and according to the Commission, it will not recognise the continued delivery of the LLB programme in a mode that has not been duly approved. This was contained in a letter dated October 5, 2026, addressed to the Vice-Chancellor of UDS in Tamale. The Deputy Director-General of GTEC, Prof Augustine Ocloo, signed the letter on behalf of the Director-General of GTEC. The letter, a copy of which has been seen by Graphic Online indicated that GTEC had noted “with serious concern that the University is currently delivering its Bachelor of Laws (LLB) programme, which was accredited for evening delivery, as a weekend programme.” It said the Commission has further established that students duly admitted to the approved evening programme are being required to migrate to the weekend mode of delivery. GTEC therefore reminded the university that the accreditation was granted on the basis of the specific academic, staffing, infrastructural and delivery arrangements submitted by an institution and assessed and approved by the Commission. It said the mode of delivery forms an integral part of the conditions under which accreditation is granted. Consequently, an institution cannot unilaterally alter the approved mode of delivery of an accredited programme without the prior written approval of the Commission. It said the conversion of an accredited evening programme into a weekend programme without prior approval therefore constitutes a material departure from the conditions of accreditation and regulatory non-compliance. It added that the Commission was particularly concerned that such an alteration has implications for academic contact hours, availability of faculty, access to teaching and learning facilities, quality assurance arrangements and the conditions under which students accepted admission into the programme. “Accordingly, the Commission hereby DIRECTS the University to CEASE, WITH IMMEDIATE EFFECT, the delivery of the accredited evening LLB programme as a weekend programme and to restore the programme to its duly approved evening mode of delivery.” The commission indicated that failure to comply within the stipulated period will constitute continued breach of the conditions under which accreditation was granted and will compel the Commission to initiate appropriate regulatory action against the programme. Such action may include the suspension or withdrawal/revocation of the programme’s accreditation, a directive to cease further admission of students into the programme, and any other regulatory measures available to the Commission under the applicable regulatory framework. It said for the avoidance of doubt, the Commission will not recognise the continued delivery of the LLB programme in a mode that has not been duly approved. The University is therefore strongly advised to treat this matter with the utmost urgency and seriousness and to ensure strict compliance within the stated period and be advised that failure to comply with this directive within seven (7) days may result in regulatory action without further notice to the university.

items.title: 2027: Abdulsalami-led Peace Committee cautions Tinubu, Atiku, Obi over inciting rhetoric
items.description: The National Peace Committee, chaired by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, has cautioned President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and other political actors against inflammatory rhetoric and inciting campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections. The committee also raised concerns over 60 election-related incidents recorded across the country within one month, including political violence, intimidation, threats, attacks on political activities and misinformation. The warning was contained in a statement jointly signed by Abubakar and the committee’s convenor, Most Rev. Matthew Kukah, on Monday. The committee urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to immediately stop the spread of false or inflammatory information and prevent acts capable of disrupting the electoral process. “To political parties, candidates, and supporters: Immediately stop false, inflammatory or inciting communication. Uphold the commitments of the Accord, verify information before publication, and actively prevent supporters from engaging in unlawful conduct, intimidation, or disruption,” the statement said. The committee stressed that all political actors must be allowed to campaign and organise peacefully, while citizens should be able to make their electoral choices without coercion. It also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to strengthen monitoring of political campaigns and enforce provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 and other regulations governing campaign conduct. The NPC further urged security agencies to intensify investigations into electoral offences and political violence. “The Committee reminds all signatories that the National Peace Accord is a solemn public commitment, not a ceremonial declaration,” it said. The warning followed the committee’s monitoring of political conduct between August 19 and September 19 through its Election Security Information Hub. According to the committee, misinformation and disinformation accounted for the largest share of the incidents, with 24 cases representing 40 per cent of the total. It recorded 13 incidents involving attacks and disruptions of political activities and assets, while 10 cases involved political intimidation and threats. Political violence and thuggery accounted for six incidents, while four cases involved inflammatory statements. The committee also recorded one case each of restriction on freedom of expression, intra-party conflict and voter inducement. items.title: We must address the role of boys in impregnating young girls, not just blame girls – Kobby Kyei
items.description: Ghanaian media personality and social commentator Kobby Kyei has called for a broader conversation about teenage pregnancy, arguing that society must pay greater attention to the role of men who impregnate young girls. Speaking with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes , Kobby Kyei said discussions surrounding teenage pregnancy often place much of the blame on girls while overlooking the men involved. According to him, in many cases, young girls are impregnated by older men, yet society quickly points fingers at the girls, labels them as wayward, and stigmatizes them while the men go free without any consequences. He described the situation as unfair and hypocritical, noting that many teenage mothers are forced to drop out of school, their future is destroyed, and they are shamed by their own communities, while those responsible for the pregnancies continue with their lives. “We must address the role of men in impregnating young girls instead of placing the blame solely on the girls. We need to be intentional about raising boys. We need to change the narrative of paying attention to the boychild ” he stated. Kobby Kyei believes the issue should be approached from both sides, with attention given to the responsibilities of men and the circumstances that lead to young girls becoming pregnant. “In the quest to empower the boy child, I tell them that we need to carry the girls along when I go to the schools because both genders move together. You can’t go to the schools to empower the girls and leave the boys. Who are they going to have the sex with?” The humanitarian quizzed. He called on parents, traditional leaders, and law enforcement agencies to hold men accountable and to strengthen systems that protect young girls from exploitation, abuse, and predatory behavior. He further argued that addressing teenage pregnancy effectively requires more than just preaching abstinence to girls. Ghana, he said, must have honest conversations about poverty, lack of protection, peer pressure, and the power imbalance that makes young girls vulnerable. His comments have sparked conversations about accountability, child protection, and the need for society to address the root factors contributing to teenage pregnancies in Ghana. Kobby Kyei’s position is that tackling the menace needs a more balanced approach; one that ensures greater responsibility from men while also creating a safer environment for young girls to grow and thrive.

items.description: El último tira y afloja por la amnistía del procés —qué ponencia iba a convertirse en la primera sentencia—se ha resuelto. La ponencia del presidente del Tribunal Constitucional, Cándido Conde-Pumpido, que avala amnistiar la malversación de los independentistas catalanes , será la primera sentencia que se apruebe en el Pleno de este martes, según fuentes del tribunal. El magistrado del bloque conservador, José María Macías, a quien hasta ahora correspondía la cabecera en el orden de los recursos , no someterá a votación su propuesta de sentencia. La ponencia del presidente fijará así la doctrina del tribunal de garantías en la materia y despejará el camino para el regreso del expresidente de la Generalitat Carles Puigdemont y los otros dos políticos fugados. items.title: Richard Nagbe Koon, vice-président du Parlement libérien en Guinée : « Nos frontières doivent être des ponts, pas des barrières »
items.description: Ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, l’Assemblée nationale de la République de Guinée a officiellement ouvert la première session de la 10ᵉ législature. Organisée dans la salle des Congrès du Palais du peuple, la cérémonie a été marquée par la présence de plusieurs délégations parlementaires étrangères, dont celle du Libéria, conduite par le vice-président de l’Assemblée nationale, Richard Nagbe Koon. « Nos frontières doivent être des ponts, pas des barrières, mais des ponts correctement gérés et sécurisés. C’est pourquoi la mise en place du Parlement de l’Union du fleuve Mano doit désormais passer de la déclaration à la mise en œuvre.“ Au nom du gouvernement et du peuple libériens, ainsi qu’en son nom propre, le représentant du Parlement libérien a adressé ses vives félicitations aux autorités guinéennes, avant de mettre l’accent sur plusieurs enjeux communs aux pays de la sous-région, notamment la sécurité aux frontières, l’immigration, la traite des êtres humains, le trafic illicite de migrants et l’insécurité. « Le Libéria, tout comme d’autres pays de notre région, accueille des migrants de toute l’Afrique de l’Ouest, dont environ 140 000 Burkinabè sans-papiers ou en situation irrégulière. Si la migration contribue à nos économies et à nos sociétés, l’immigration clandestine peut engendrer des difficultés en matière de gestion des frontières, de sécurité, de fiscalité, de réglementation du travail et d’accès aux services publics » « La Guinée, le Libéria, la Sierra Leone et la Côte d’Ivoire partagent des frontières, une histoire, des familles, des cultures et des marchés. Ce lien constitue une force, mais il représente également des défis communs, tels que l’immigration frontalière, la traite des êtres humains, le trafic illicite des migrants, l’insécurité, le commerce informel, le chômage et la faiblesse des infrastructures frontalières », a-t-il déclaré. Abordant plus particulièrement la question migratoire, Richard Nagbe Koon a estimé que cette problématique mérite une attention particulière. « Le Libéria, tout comme d’autres pays de notre région, accueille des migrants de toute l’Afrique de l’Ouest, dont environ 140 000 Burkinabè sans-papiers ou en situation irrégulière. Si la migration contribue à nos économies et à nos sociétés, l’immigration clandestine peut engendrer des difficultés en matière de gestion des frontières, de sécurité, de fiscalité, de réglementation du travail et d’accès aux services publics », a-t-il souligné. Le vice-président de l’Assemblée nationale du Libéria a toutefois insisté sur la nécessité d’éviter toute attitude hostile envers les migrants. « Elle doit être ordonnée, légale, documentée et humaine, tout en protégeant la sécurité nationale et la dignité de chaque personne. Ces défis ne peuvent pas être relevés par un seul pays agissant seul. C’est là que le Parlement doit intervenir. Nos assemblées législatives peuvent renforcer les lois relatives aux migrations, à la traite des personnes, à la gestion des frontières et au commerce frontalier, exercer un contrôle plus strict sur les institutions frontalières et promouvoir des accords qui facilitent la circulation légale des personnes et des biens, tout en protégeant nos communautés », a-t-il expliqué. Par ailleurs, l’élu libérien a réaffirmé son engagement en faveur du renforcement des liens entre les États membres de l’Union du fleuve Mano. « Nos frontières doivent être des ponts, pas des barrières, mais des ponts correctement gérés et sécurisés. C’est pourquoi la mise en place du Parlement de l’Union du fleuve Mano doit désormais passer de la déclaration à la mise en œuvre. Nos présidents d’Assemblée ont déjà approuvé cette importante initiative. J’espère que les trois présidents d’Assemblée présents ici s’accorderont sur une date précise pour que notre prochaine réunion aille de l’avant afin de finaliser les formalités restantes », a-t-il déclaré. Pour finir, Richard Nagbe Koon a estimé qu’un Parlement de l’Union du fleuve Mano opérationnel pourrait jouer un rôle déterminant dans la réponse aux défis communs de la sous-région. « Un Parlement de l’Union du fleuve Mano opérationnel peut offrir à notre région une plateforme permanente pour relever les défis communs, harmoniser les législations, faciliter le commerce renforcé, la coopération frontalière et promouvoir la paix et la sécurité. Nos exécutifs négocient des accords. items.title: Mahama grants presidential pardon to 863 convicted persons
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has granted presidential pardon to 863 convicted persons as part of activities marking Ghana’s 70th Independence Anniversary. The President exercised the prerogative of mercy in accordance with Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution, following consultation with the Council of State. According to a statement issued on Monday, October 5, the pardon is intended to mark the independence anniversary with an act of mercy and national reflection. The largest group comprises 819 first offenders, who have been granted outright release, per the statement signed by Felix Kwakye Ofosu, spokesperson to the President and Minister for Government Communications. The beneficiaries also include 13 persons aged 70 years and above, who have been granted outright release, while six seriously ill persons have also been granted outright release. In addition, the death sentences of 11 convicted persons have been commuted to life imprisonment. A further six persons serving life sentences will have their sentences commuted to 20 years definite. Two persons under the special recommendation category have been granted outright release, while three petitions and three others were also approved, bringing the total number of beneficiaries to 863. The relevant state institutions have been directed to take the necessary steps to give effect to the President’s decision.

items.title: Iran president says talks with US ‘meaningless’
items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that negotiations with the United States were “meaningless” and only resulted in renewed attacks, state media reported, with progress on ending the Middle East war stalled for months. “So far, they have attacked us three times after talks, and this shows that they are not seeking dialogue; rather, their goal is to overthrow the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by the state news agency IRNA. “With an enemy that every day resorts to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats, and that breaks its commitments, negotiations are meaningless.” The Middle East war was started in late February by the US and Israel when they launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, even as Washington and Tehran were in the midst of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. The warring parties agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution to the conflict, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations. Negotiations have effectively been at an impasse since then, and recent indirect talks between the US and Iran on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly failed to produce a breakthrough. Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure, and has not struck Iran since September 1. On Sunday, Iran’s top diplomat insisted the United States’ war against the Islamic republic would not be resolved by military means. Vowing a stronger defence if any attacks resumed, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions.” “Only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict, he added. The United States and Israel have said the war is necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons — a goal it has long denied pursuing — though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Strait of Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets. Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation. The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it. A tanker was struck while attempting to transit the waterway on Sunday, while another turned back on Monday after being threatened with attack by Iranian forces, according to the British maritime agency UKMTO. AFP The post Iran president says talks with US ‘meaningless’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Jail term for preaching in commercial vehicles increased to eight months
items.description: People who preach or sell in moving commercial vehicles in Ghana risk up to eight months in prison under the new road traffic regulations. It represents a tougher punishment than the 30 days or up to 3 months’ jail term captured under the previous rules for the specified offences. The Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) prohibit causing or permitting a nuisance, including preaching and hawking, on a public or commercial vehicle while it is in motion. Under Regulation 141, an offender faces a fine of between 10 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both. With one penalty unit valued at GH¢12, the fine ranges from GH¢120 to GH¢600. The provision means that activities sometimes seen in tro-tros and buses, including religious preaching and the sale of goods to passengers while a vehicle is moving, can attract criminal penalties. What has changed? The restriction itself is not new. Regulation 116 of L.I. 2180 already prohibited a person from causing or permitting a nuisance, including preaching and hawking, on a public or commercial vehicle in motion. The significant change under Regulation 141 of L.I. 2519 is the tougher punishment. Under the old rules, an offender faced a fine of up to 50 penalty units, a prison term or both. The new regulations retain a fine range of 10 to 50 penalty units but raise the maximum custodial sentence to eight months. The change comes as the government steps up efforts to improve discipline and safety on the country’s roads. The Minister for Transport, Joseph Bukari Nikpe, launched a nationwide public education campaign in September to familiarise road users and transport operators with the Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153), and L.I. 2519. The Ministry of Transport says the new framework is intended to strengthen road safety, improve enforcement and ensure that road users understand their responsibilities. Other reforms include automated traffic enforcement, a demerit-point system linked to driving licences and tougher penalties for certain traffic offences. Why preaching and hawking are covered The regulation applies to the specified activities when a public or commercial vehicle is moving. It covers preaching and hawking as forms of nuisance and is not directed at any particular religion. The restriction also applies to people who sell goods to passengers inside moving commercial vehicles. The renewed public attention on the provision has triggered debate about religious expression, the everyday culture of public transport and the enforcement of traffic rules. However, the fact that the prohibition has existed since 2012 means the new regulations should not be interpreted as introducing an entirely new ban. Rather, they increase the possible consequences for those who breach it. The nationwide sensitisation campaign is intended to help drivers, passengers, transport operators and other road users understand the revised legal framework and comply with the rules.

items.title: State security prosecution releases journalist Rasha Azab on LE10,000 bail
items.description: Journalist Rasha Azab was released on LE10,000 bail on Monday evening by the Supreme State Security Prosecution following questioning in relation to a tweet she published in recent weeks regarding the conduct of the Interior Ministry and its impact on the public mood. She was questioned on charges of “promoting the perpetration of terrorist acts” and using a website to promote ideas calling for doing so in Supreme State Security Prosecution Case 8025/2026, her defense lawyer, Ragia Omran, told Mada Masr. Azab was questioned on her reasons for publishing a tweet, in which she wrote, on September 23, “how long does it take to go from ‘the Interior Ministry are thugs’ to ‘the people want the fall of the regime.’” Azab responded that her tweet was commentary on the case of Dina Ezzat, a woman who called for her husband’s release on social media in September, after he was arrested from their Nasr City home by authorities in their local area. Ezzat herself was briefly taken into custody after she spoke out against her husband’s arrest before she was later released on bail. According to the case’s record, 12 people filed complaints at police stations across several governorates against Azab the day after she posted her tweet, Omran said. The prosecution did not question her about the Matsda2sh case. Azab herself, however, pointed to what she had read on social media regarding the Matsda2sh journalists’ complaints of torture at National Security Agency headquarters , when prosecutors asked her for examples of “thuggery” on the part of the Interior Minsitry. She also cited her own subjection to assault during a 2024 protest outside the United Nations Women office, after which she was briefly arrested before being released on bail, as well as threats, pursuit and the theft of her car; incidents she said her local police station had refused to allow her to file a report on. During the investigation, Azab said that she did not know the Matsda2sh journalists previously and that she knew of them and of their arrest through the statements published by the Journalists Syndicate, and that she had heard that they were tortured in custody via published statements. Azab received a summons to the prosecution on Saturday, without explanation of the charges or the incidents under investigation, and was presented on Monday afternoon for questioning. She posted to her X account earlier on Monday that she views herself as “once again accused,” after two years of harassment which included her hounding, the theft of her car in 2024 and the “destruction of her life.” She added that the summons comes during a time of an ongoing push for “independent journalism and a nation without despotism,” and called for the support of her colleagues present today at the Journalists Syndicate. The summons came in the wake of an ongoing demonstration at the syndicate, in which Azab had participated, along with dozens of other journalists, in solidarity with the six from independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh who were arrested last week. Upon receiving the summons, her lawyers inquired about the case against her and found that it predated the campaign targeting the Matsda2sh team. The post State security prosecution releases journalist Rasha Azab on LE10,000 bail first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Diplomatie : Devant l’Assemblée nationale guinéenne, le CNT malien magnifie la fraternité « séculaire » entre Bamako et Conakry
items.description: C’est un plaidoyer vibrant pour la souveraineté retrouvée et la solidarité ouest-africaine qu’a livré ce lundi l'honorable Diarra Raky Talla, deuxième vice-présidente du Conseil national de la transition (CNT) du Mali. Prenant la parole devant l’Assemblée nationale de la République de Guinée lors de sa session solennelle, la cheffe de la délégation parlementaire malienne a célébré l'axe Bamako-Conakry, le qualifiant de rempart face aux crises sous-régionales. ​Devant les députés guinéens et de nombreux dignitaires, la deuxième vice-présidente du Conseil national de la transition (CNT) du Mali a réaffirmé que l'union entre le Mali et la Guinée dépasse le simple cadre géographique ou administratif. Évoquant le legs de Modibo Keïta et d’Ahmed Sékou Touré, elle a rappelé que les deux nations partagent une histoire et une vision communes depuis les premières heures des indépendances. ​« Notre génération et celles à venir auront toujours comme boussole cette citation célèbre de feu le président Ahmed Sékou Touré : “Nous préférons la pauvreté dans la liberté à l'opulence dans l'esclavage” », a déclaré l'honorable Diarra Raky Talla, établissant un lien direct entre ce combat historique et les orientations données par les présidents Assimi Goïta et Mamadi Doumbouya. ​La gratitude de Bamako face aux sanctions ​Moment fort de cette intervention : la reconnaissance explicite du Mali envers la position adoptée par Conakry lors du blocus économique imposé à Bamako par la CEDEAO. La vice-présidente du CNT a souligné que le peuple malien « n'oubliera jamais la position courageuse et fraternelle » de la Guinée, qui avait refusé de fermer ses frontières avec son voisin. Ce geste de solidarité, posé dans une période critique, demeure gravé dans la mémoire collective malienne comme une preuve concrète d’un partenariat indéfectible. ​ Sécurité et « diplomatie des peuples » ​Au-delà de l'hommage historique, la cheffe de la délégation malienne a abordé les défis urgents de la sous-région, en premier lieu la lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité transfrontalière. Face à ces menaces, le CNT appelle à une synergie sécuritaire renforcée et à un rôle accru des Parlements. ​Definissant la diplomatie parlementaire comme une « diplomatie des peuples » capable de maintenir le dialogue là où la diplomatie classique des États échoue, l’intervenante a partagé les réformes institutionnelles menées à Bamako (transparence, régulation interne, déontologie) tout en saluant les initiatives de modernisation engagées par l'Assemblée nationale guinéenne sous la conduite du Dr Dansa Kourouma. ​Maliens et Guinéens entendent ainsi faire de la coopération interparlementaire un levier majeur pour stabiliser la région et bâtir une Afrique « solidaire, prospère et pleinement maîtresse de son destin ».

items.title: Formation du gouvernement : Mansouri consulte Benabdallah et ouvre les discussions avec Lachgar
items.description: Une source dirigeante du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) a indiqué que Fatima Zahra Mansouri, désignée pour diriger le gouvernement et chargée de sa formation, a tenu, ce lundi matin, une réunion avec Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah, secrétaire général du Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS). Le comité central de ce dernier doit se réunir demain, mardi, en session extraordinaire afin de se prononcer sur une éventuelle participation au gouvernement. De même, Driss Lachgar de l'USFP était attendu au siège du PAM pour tenir une réunion. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre des consultations pour la formation du gouvernement, qui devraient se poursuivre avec d’autres partis que Mansouri choisira en concertation avec la commission chargée de cette mission par le bureau politique, a indiqué une source dirigeante au sein du PAM. Les estimations indiquent par ailleurs que Mansouri souhaiterait mettre en place un nouveau gouvernement politique fondé sur une alliance avec les partis de la Koutla nationale, à savoir le Parti de l’Istiqlal, le Parti du progrès et du socialisme et l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP). La même source a précisé que les autres partis politiques ont tenu, durant le week-end, les sessions extraordinaires de leurs conseils nationaux. Le « Parti du Livre » (PPS) doit pour sa part réunir son comité central en session extraordinaire afin de présenter le bilan des consultations menées avec Mansouri, lors de la première comme de la deuxième tournée. Le comité pourra ainsi en débattre, puisqu’il constitue la plus haute instance décisionnelle du parti, à l’image du conseil national dans d’autres formations politiques. Une autre source a révélé qu’une réunion de la commission relevant du bureau politique du PAM, chargée de conduire les consultations, est prévue ce lundi soir. Elle devra présenter le bilan de la rencontre avec Benabdallah. Selon cette source, « la configuration finale du gouvernement semble désormais claire pour Mansouri ; mais sa validation et sa présentation au Roi Mohammed VI, qui l’a nommée à la tête du gouvernement, seront déterminantes avant son annonce officielle ». Selon la première configuration envisagée, la majorité gouvernementale pourrait être élargie numériquement avec l’entrée de l’Union constitutionnelle (UC) ou du Mouvement populaire (MP), aux côtés des partis de la Koutla. La participation du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) reste toutefois incertaine, plusieurs partis ayant posé leur « veto » à sa participation, parmi lesquels le Parti du progrès et du socialisme. Un membre du bureau politique du PPS a déclaré que les échanges entre Mansouri et le secrétaire général du « Parti du Livre » constitueront une base de discussion lors de la session extraordinaire du comité central. Il a précisé que « toute coordination dans le cadre des consultations sur la coalition gouvernementale tient compte du parcours du parti et de son expérience dans la majorité comme dans l’opposition, afin qu’il puisse jouer un rôle actif, qu’il participe au gouvernement ou qu’il choisisse de rejoindre l’opposition ». Dans le même sillage, Driss Lachgar, premier secrétaire de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), a été aperçu à l’entrée du siège du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), ce lundi soir, dans le cadre des consultations en cours pour la formation du gouvernement. Cette présence vient renforcer les informations dont dispose le journal concernant la possibilité de former une alliance avec les partis de la Koutla nationale démocratique. Selon des sources bien informées, Fatima Zahra Mansouri, secrétaire générale du PAM, est également arrivée au siège du parti, où elle devrait s’entretenir avec Lachgar au sujet des évolutions politiques liées aux consultations pour la formation du gouvernement. Des sources concordantes au sein du PAM indiquent que cette alliance pourrait réunir le Parti de l’Istiqlal, le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS) et l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), avec l’ajout éventuel d’un autre parti afin d’élargir numériquement la coalition. The post Formation du gouvernement : Mansouri consulte Benabdallah et ouvre les discussions avec Lachgar appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tema Central MP assaulted my driver – Ebi Bright alleges
items.description: Tema Metropolitan Chief Executive Ebi Bright has alleged that Tema Central Member of Parliament Charles Forson physically assaulted her driver during an attempt to engage him on development issues in the municipality. Speaking on Monday, October 5, Ms Bright said Mr Forson had consistently declined to engage her or the Tema Metropolitan Assembly since she assumed office, despite several attempts to establish communication with him. “To be honest, the MP has been resolute in not engaging me or the Assembly since I came into office,” she said. She said the lack of engagement had become a concern because some of the issues before the Assembly required discussions with the MP to ensure that development efforts were properly coordinated. “Some of the issues that have reached my table have required a discussion because unfortunately we’re not concerted in what we’re doing,” she said. According to Ms Bright, the lack of coordination had also resulted in duplication, with some projects already captured in the Assembly’s annual action plans being undertaken separately. She said coordination was particularly necessary for projects involving government reserve and open spaces, where the Assembly needed to engage relevant stakeholders before implementation. “Some of the issues have been to implement projects on government reserve open spaces, and you want to have a conversation, but he’s been resolute in not stepping into the Assembly or engaging my office,” she said. Ms Bright said she had made several attempts to reach Mr Forson, with the support of other individuals, including some leaders in Parliament. “I have made, with the support of other individuals, including some leadership in Parliament, attempts to approach him,” she said. She alleged that the latest of those attempts, made at Parliament, ended with her driver being physically assaulted. “The last of such efforts was met with physical assault on my driver because we tried to reach him at Parliament and we couldn’t reach him,” she alleged. Further attempt to meet MP Ms Bright said she later went to Mr Forson’s residence, which she said was opposite her private office, but was unable to gain access to him. She said she subsequently sent a package to his office to greet him and request a meeting, but alleged that the encounter also resulted in a member of her staff being assaulted. Ms Bright said the matter had since come to the attention of some parliamentary leaders, and expressed hope that it would be resolved. “So this has also come to the attention of some leadership in Parliament, and we’re hoping to resolve those issues,” adding that the MP “has been resolute and not engaging.” She said the attempts to engage Mr Forson were intended to improve coordination on development projects and prevent duplication within the municipality.

items.title: Nigeria needs leaders to stop oppression — Datti Baba-Ahmed
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The former Labour Party vice-presidential candidate, Datti Baba-Ahmed, has called for leaders capable of ending oppression in Nigeria, saying the practice was becoming entrenched in the country’s leadership and society. Baba-Ahmed spoke on Monday while delivering a keynote address at the second edition of the Bala AbdulKadir Mohammed Colloquium, held at the Ahmadu Bello International Conference Centre, Bauchi, to commemorate the 68th birthday of Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed. He said Nigerians needed leaders who would stand for the people, protect their rights and ensure that oppression did not become entrenched in the country. He said, “Nigeria needs leaders that will stop oppression. Do you remember that there is a saying about injustice and helping the oppressed and the oppressor? “How do you help someone who is oppressing? You stop him from oppressing. That is what we need to begin to do because now oppression is getting into the DNA of Nigerian leaders and the Nigerian people.” The former vice presidential candidate also urged Nigerians to take responsibility for demanding good governance, defending their rights and participating actively in the democratic process. Baba-Ahmed said, “Why can’t the Nigerian people come together? Why can’t the Nigerian people think for themselves, fend for themselves, stand for themselves and fight for themselves?” He said democracy must remain centred on the welfare and interests of the people, while questioning whether Nigeria’s democratic system was adequately serving citizens. Baba-Ahmed also criticised the lack of independence and diversity in the Nigerian Senate, saying lawmakers faced a difficult choice between representing the executive and representing the people. He said, “The Nigerian Senate has struggled for independence. It has been denied variety and vibrancy. It struggles to know who it represents: is it the almighty executive led by the president, or the people? “This third point is, in fact, too fundamental because unless where you have people like Bala and my humble self who tend to enforce their independence across then you will have to make a clear choice: you will represent your boss, your benefactor, and your leader. “If you represent the people, you are at risk; your seat is at risk.” He further called for forgiveness, unity and trust among Nigerians, saying citizens should recognise the positive contributions of leaders without turning such appreciation into sycophancy. He said, “When you appreciate leaders, it is not to massage them. What is even more important is to educate others to appreciate and understand, and take an example, even if it is one single quality from that leader.” Baba-Ahmed also reflected on his involvement in the 2023 general election, saying he did not regret supporting what he described as the defence of Nigerians’ constitutional rights. He urged Nigerians to learn from the country’s political history and ensure that future leadership remained focused on the interests and welfare of the people. Also speaking at the event, a former National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Kabiru Turaki, called for improved quality of representation and legislation in the National Assembly. Turaki said lawmakers should focus on making laws that would positively affect the lives of ordinary Nigerians rather than increasing the burden on citizens. He said, “Every day, laws are being turned out of the National Assembly. Every day, legislation is made. But the question is, do these legislations fundamentally affect the lives of the common man in this country? “We need legislation that will add value positively to the lives of Nigerians. Legislation that will tackle the problem of unemployment, poverty and insecurity that we are facing today.” Turaki criticised what he described as legislation that placed additional burdens on Nigerians, saying lawmakers should be more responsive to the challenges confronting citizens. He also urged young Nigerians to become actively involved in politics and governance, rejecting the notion that the youth should simply wait for their turn to lead. He said, “They will tell you, ‘Youths of today are the leaders of tomorrow.’ You are 28; you will even get to 68. When will that tomorrow come?” Turaki urged Nigerians from different sectors of society to participate in politics and the democratic process, warning that the withdrawal of credible and experienced individuals from politics could create room for people without integrity or credibility to take over leadership positions. He said traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil servants, businesspeople and other respected members of society should take an interest in political affairs and elections. He added that citizens had a responsibility to monitor elected officials and demand accountability from those entrusted with public offices. Turaki said, “It is only by doing so that we will unlock the process. And when we unlock it, then we have the legal and moral right to call those we elected into responsibility.” The post Nigeria needs leaders to stop oppression — Datti Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Vanguard News .
